G.A.

Hon'Ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav, J.
Heard learned counsel for the appellants, learned A.G.A. for the State, and perused the record.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A(1) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (in short, "the SC/ST Act") has been preferred by the appellants seeking to quash the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 1818 of 2022 (State vs. Ganga Prasad @ Ballu and others), pending before the Court of the Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Pilibhit, as well as to set aside the cognizance/summoning order dated 28.05.2024 passed in the said case, which arose out of Protest Petition No. 921 of 2022 in Case Crime No. 269 of 2022, under Sections 376-D, 504,
506 IPC and Sections 3(1)(w)(i), 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act, Police Station Neoria, District Pilibhit.

sentences.text:
The contention of learned counsel for the appellants is that the allegations are false and motivated;
that no offence is disclosed against the appellants; and that the entire prosecution has been instituted with mala fide intent for the purpose of harassment.
It is submitted that the learned court below has passed the impugned summoning order mechanically, without due application of judicial mind.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. has opposed the appeal and contended that at the stage of summoning,
the Magistrate or the Special Court is only required to consider whether, on a prima facie view of the material available, there exist sufficient grounds to proceed against the accused.
The impugned order, being a reasoned one, does not suffer from any illegality or infirmity warranting interference by this Court.

Having considered the rival submissions and upon perusal of the material on record, it is apparent that the learned Special Judge, upon a detailed consideration of the final report submitted by the Investigating Officer and the protest petition filed by the victim, found that there was prima facie material to take cognizance against the appellants under Sections 376-D/34 IPC and Sections 3(1)(w)(i) and 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act.

The learned court below has recorded reasons based upon the statements of the victim under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., and the material on record, for rejecting the final report and summoning the accused.
At this stage, this Court cannot enter into disputed questions of fact or assess the correctness or veracity of the allegations.
The law is well settled that while exercising jurisdiction to quash criminal proceedings or summoning orders, the Court must see only whether a prima facie case is made out.

Reference may be made to R.P. Kapur vs. State of Punjab, AIR 1960 SC 866; State of Haryana vs.
Ram Singh And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102011717/
2 Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335; State of Bihar vs. P.P. Sharma, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 222; and Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. vs. Mohd. Sharaful Haque, (2005) 1 SCC 122.

sentences.text: The disputed defence of the appellants cannot be adjudicated upon at this stage.

They will have adequate opportunity to raise all such pleas, including those relating to false implication or mala fide, before the trial court in appropriate proceedings, such as an application for discharge.
Accordingly, the prayer for quashing the proceedings of Criminal Case No. 1818 of 2022 and the impugned summoning order dated 28.05.2024 is refused.
However, it is provided that if the appellants move discharge applications before the trial court, the same shall be considered and decided in accordance with law, expeditiously.
With the aforesaid observations and directions, the present criminal appeal stands finally disposed of.
